title: Replace Command with Function

solutions.title: One function, no ceremony
solutions.tradeoff: calculateHandlingFee can no longer keep a partial calculation alive between two calls the way an unexecuted command object could - not that anything in this module ever did, which is the whole point.

reviewFocus: Count CalculateHandlingFeeCommand's fields against its constructor parameters. If every field is just a stored constructor argument, does the walkthrough say so plainly, or does it hedge?
Does calculateHandlingFee still take the same single Order parameter the command's constructor took, or did the refactoring quietly change what a caller has to supply?
Do handlingFeeFor, formatFeeLine and totalWithFee still exist under the same names with the same behaviour, now calling a function instead of instantiating and executing a command?
Does the walkthrough admit that handlingFeeFor is now a one-line pass-through itself - and say why it stays rather than getting inlined away?

Compare against drill-11-09: does this walkthrough's reasoning for collapsing the class actually contradict 11-09's reasoning for building one, or are they applying the same test to a case that fails it?
